description: qou-99qc: the augmentation and convention D are Wenzl levels r=1 and r=2 of one family. z(r) = q^(2r-1)(q^2-1)/(q^(2r)-1), derived by solving the corpus's own Wenzl relation. The row cap (Orellana Crelle 508 p.5) then gives one-row support at r=1 and two-row at r=2 FOR EVERY n, removing the n=3-only caveat of #7115 (13bb8243d87). Admissibility = r<=2, so exactly two admissible levels at every n; the published z=1 is a non-integer level. Scope-(a); chooses no level and wires nothing.

checks.name: wenzl_relation_SOLVES_to_a_closed_form_in_the_level
checks.detail: solving Q^r = z_W/(1-Q+z_W) for z with Q=q^2, z_W=qz gives z(r) = q**(2*r - 1)*(q**2 - 1)/(q**(2*r) - 1) -- derived from the corpus's own relation, not assumed

checks.name: level_1_IS_the_augmentation
checks.detail: z(1) = q exactly -- the augmentation sigma -> q, which #7115 showed is the Markov trace at that parameter

checks.name: level_2_IS_convention_D
checks.detail: z(2) = q^3/(q^2+1) = z_D exactly. D7's characterisation of D as the two-row TL truncation is DERIVED here from the corpus's Wenzl relation rather than taken on trust

checks.name: level_1_supports_EXACTLY_the_one_row_partition_for_every_n
checks.detail: n = 3:[(3,)], 4:[(4,)], 5:[(5,)], 6:[(6,)], 7:[(7,)] -- one row at every n, so the augmentation's ONE-row cap is structural and not the n=3 accident #7115 could not exclude

checks.name: level_2_supports_EXACTLY_the_two_row_family_for_every_n
checks.detail: at every n the nonzero weights are exactly the lambda with l(lambda) <= 2, i.e. D7's family lambda = (n-k, k) -- Orellana Crelle 508 (1999) p.5, s_{alpha,r} = 0 for l(alpha) > r

checks.name: the_two_supports_are_STRICTLY_NESTED_at_every_n
checks.detail: one-row is a PROPER subset of two-row at every n, so the augmentation is a strict refinement of convention D and is not D -- #7115's conclusion, now general

checks.name: CALIBRATION_reproduces_the_merged_n3_weight_table
checks.detail: r=1 gives y_(3)=1, y_(2,1)=0, y_(1^3)=0 and r=2 gives ((q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, q^2/(q^2+1)^2, 0) -- byte-for-byte the table in #7115 (13bb8243d87), so this route is anchored to the merged result rather than free-standing

checks.name: admissibility_is_EXACTLY_level_le_2_hence_two_roots_at_every_n
checks.detail: level 3 gives a NONZERO weight on a 3-row block (n=3: y_(1,1,1) != 0), so it is inadmissible; with the row cap this makes 'annihilates >= 3 rows' equivalent to r <= 2. The two admissible roots the corpus found at n=3 are the two integer levels 1 and 2, and there are two of them at EVERY n -- not a coincidence of one cubic

checks.name: published_z_eq_1_sits_at_a_NON_INTEGER_wenzl_level
checks.detail: r = 1.12388310382 at the proton pin -- strictly between levels 1 and 2 and not an integer. A non-integer level is not a level, so no row cap applies and z=1 annihilates NOTHING. That is the general-n form of the inadmissibility #7115 established at n=3 by a numerator not vanishing

caveats: Scope-(a). Establishes a structural identification and a support fact; derives no observable and proposes no value.

It does NOT choose the level. D7 does, by scoping convention D (level 2) to the decay/Q_beta channel -- and whether that scoping reaches the choice of functional WITHIN the channel is the owner's reading, still open.
Level 2 gives -43.157 %, the WORSE of the two residuals. That is the anti-fitting directive working, not a defect.
Option E (derive a different element Delta) is untouched and remains the only route to a parameter-free admissible sub-1 % result (qou-37j2).
The row cap is cited from Orellana Crelle 508 (1999) p.5 via the corpus's WenzlWeightVanishing.lean; it is not re-proved here.
Supports are checked at n = 3..7. The cap itself is general, but the computation is not a proof for all n.
